reasons.local-glm: It does hand a slice to json.loads and guards JSONDecodeError, but the manual brace-counting acts as a non-JSON grammar authority that miscounts braces inside string literals (e.g. {"a": "}"}), and the loop raises an IndexError instead of returning None on unbalanced input like '{'.
reasons.gpt-5.5: The candidate uses json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode as the grammar authority (no regex), scans candidate '{' positions, guards JSONDecodeError, returns the first parsed dict, and returns None on non-dict/failure — meeting the criterion and even handling trailing prose more robustly than the reference.
reasons.zai-glm-flash: The candidate uses json.JSONDecoder.raw_decode as the grammar authority (no regex), scans from each '{' candidate, guards JSONDecodeError via its ValueError superclass, and returns None on non-dict or failure—actually handling trailing prose more robustly than the reference.

reasons.gpt-5.5: The candidate correctly identifies memory pressure and preserved computation semantics, but hedges the mechanism among several possibilities rather than clearly attributing the slowdown to CPU/RAM offload of model layers.
reasons.oc-glm: The candidate correctly attributes the slowdown to offloading weights/KV cache to system RAM when VRAM is insufficient, but only notes that output remains correct without explaining that correctness is preserved because the same weights are used.
reasons.zai-glm-flash: The candidate correctly attributes the slowdown to offloading weights to system RAM when VRAM is insufficient (with plausible added detail about PCIe transfer and KV-cache pressure) and explicitly notes correctness is preserved because the same computation runs, satisfying both parts of the criterion.

reasons.local-glm: The mechanism (background-tab timer/event-loop throttling) is correctly identified, but the mitigation—offloading to a Web Worker—is a partial workaround that doesn't match the criterion's mitigations (keep tab visible or disable throttling flags) and wouldn't fix rAF-driven stalls or be applicable when the page code can't be modified.
reasons.gpt-5.5: The candidate correctly identifies background-tab throttling (timer/event-loop clamping via page visibility) as the mechanism and provides valid mitigations (keep tab visible or launch Chrome with throttling-disabling flags), fully meeting the criterion.
reasons.oc-glm: The mechanism (background-tab throttling with timer clamping and rAF suspension) is correctly identified, but the Web Worker mitigation, while technically real for timer throttling, is not practical for an eval harness that doesn't control the page's code and differs from the criterion's mitigations (keep tab visible or disable throttling flags).
reasons.zai-glm-flash: The candidate correctly identifies background-tab throttling (timer clamping and rAF suspension for hidden tabs) as the mechanism and provides valid mitigations including the Chrome throttling-disable flags and keeping the tab foregrounded, fully meeting the criterion.

reasons.gpt-5.5: The candidate correctly explains that pkill -f matches the controlling shell's own command line (e.g., sh -c containing the pattern) causing self-termination, and recommends killing by explicit tracked PID/process group instead of command-line matching, fully satisfying the criterion.
reasons.oc-glm: The candidate correctly explains that pkill -f matches the full command line including the controlling shell's own arguments (causing self-kill), and recommends explicit-PID killing—both by capturing $! at launch and by pgrep filtering that excludes self ($$) and parent ($PPID)—fully meeting the criterion.
reasons.zai-glm-flash: The candidate correctly explains that pkill -f matches the full command line of the invoking shell (causing it to be signaled and exit 143) and recommends explicit-PID killing via capturing $! instead of pattern matching, fully meeting the criterion.
